title: Returned Payments and the Certified-Funds Period on Vehicle Purchase Agreements
content:
**Returned payments.** On the **Vehicle Purchase Agreements**, when the bank returns a check or ACH payment, its credit is taken back by a returned-payment entry that points at the payment. The deal type's returned payment fee is posted on the same date. A disputed card payment (a chargeback) is taken back the same way but draws no returned payment fee.

**Certified-funds period.** After a returned payment the customer enters a certified-funds period on all of their deals. During that period, a payment by check, ACH or credit card is accepted only when the handling date is later than the latest returned payment date plus the deal type's certified-funds days. Payments in cash, by cashier's check or by debit card are accepted at any time.

**Counting.** Calendar days are added to the date of the customer's latest returned payment, taken across all of that customer's deals. The period covers the boundary day itself, so check, ACH and credit card payments are accepted from the next calendar day.

## Input — judgement — result (hypothetical: 60 certified-funds days, counted from the date of the latest returned payment)

| Payment offered | Handling date | Result |
|---|---|---|
| check | 60 calendar days after the latest return | not accepted: the boundary day is inside the period |
| ACH | 61 calendar days after the latest return | accepted |
| debit card | any date | accepted |
| cashier's check | 1 calendar day after the latest return | accepted |

| Payment taken back | Returned payment fee |
|---|---|
| check returned unpaid | posted on the same date |
| ACH returned unpaid | posted on the same date |
| card chargeback | none |
